sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.text:
Make an animation that, if everyone watched it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.

Deliver the result as image and/or video files, working in the current directory.
- Save the finished files in ./output/. Only what is in ./output/ is published as the result, so
  ./output/ holds those finished image/video files and nothing else.
- Formats: images as .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or .svg; videos as .mp4 or .webm. At most 8 files,
  each under 2 MB; videos at most 10 seconds.
- To check your work, look at what you made (a still, a rendered frame, a few frames of the video), and
  save what you look at as .jpg rather than .png: each image you read stays in your context, and a long
  session of large .png files can hit the provider's per-request image limit and end the run.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.12.13 (standard library only), node 24.18.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 8.1.1, ffprobe 8.1.1. Don't install packages or download anything.
- Keep the code you write to make the files in the working directory (its root, or a subdirectory
  like ./src/, but not in ./output/): it's published as the source. Delete intermediate files such
  as rendered frames when you're done.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

def draw_earth(buf, R, rot, t):
    invR = 1.0 / R
    R2 = R * R
    GR = R * 1.13
    GR2 = GR * GR
    x0 = max(0, int(CX - GR))
    x1 = min(W - 1, int(CX + GR) + 1)
    y0 = max(0, int(CY - GR))
    y1 = min(H - 1, int(CY + GR) + 1)
    base_b = rot * 0.2 + 36.0 + 720.0        # lon -> map col (multiple-of-72 offset)
    cloud_b = rot * 1.15 * 0.4 + 72.0 + 1440.0
    asin_, sqrt_ = math.asin, math.sqrt
    LXl, LYl, LZl = LX, LY, LZ

        dy = y - CY

        if alat > 59.0:

        else:

        lr = 52.0 + (168.0 - 52.0) * dw
        lg = 84.0 + (146.0 - 84.0) * dw
        lb = 52.0 + (100.0 - 52.0) * dw
        lr += (225.0 - lr) * sw
        lg += (232.0 - lg) * sw
        lb += (240.0 - lb) * sw

                if cl > 1.0:
                    cl = 1.0

                    else:
                        q = (land - 0.35) / 0.27
                        la = q * q * (3.0 - 2.0 * q)

                    cg = og + (lg - og) * la
                    cb = ob + (lb - ob) * la
                else:

                gv = cg * li + 5.0 * (1.0 - day)
                bv = cb * li + 12.0 * (1.0 - day)

                if cl > 0.02:                    # clouds
                    cw = cl * 0.62
                    clb = 0.10 + 0.90 * day
                    rv += (235.0 * clb - rv) * cw
                    gv += (242.0 * clb - gv) * cw
                    bv += (249.0 * clb - bv) * cw

                if n2 > 0.88:                    # atmospheric limb
                    hq = (n2 - 0.88) / 0.12
                    if hq > 1.0:
                        hq = 1.0
                    hq = hq * hq * (3.0 - 2.0 * hq)
                    hz = hq * 0.30 * (0.25 + 0.75 * day)
                    rv += (150.0 - rv) * hz
                    gv += (200.0 - gv) * hz
                    bv += (255.0 - bv) * hz

                i = rowstart + (x - x0) * 3
                buf[i] = 255 if rv > 255 else int(rv)
                buf[i + 1] = 255 if gv > 255 else int(gv)
                buf[i + 2] = 255 if bv > 255 else int(bv)
            else:

                    lit = ux * LXl + uy * LYl

                    gb = a2 * (0.32 + 0.68 * lit) * 0.55
                    i = rowstart + (x - x0) * 3

                    buf[i] = 255 if v > 255 else int(v)
                    v = buf[i + 1] + 180.0 * gb
                    buf[i + 1] = 255 if v > 255 else int(v)
                    v = buf[i + 2] + 255.0 * gb
                    buf[i + 2] = 255 if v > 255 else int(v)

                i = rowb + x * 3
                v = buf[i] + (225.0 * core + 115.0 * halo) * gA
                buf[i] = 255 if v > 255 else int(v)
                v = buf[i + 1] + (240.0 * core + 175.0 * halo) * gA
                buf[i + 1] = 255 if v > 255 else int(v)

Done. In `./output/`:

- **`pale_blue_dot.mp4`** (10.0 s, 800×450, 427 KB) — the animation
- **`poster_earth.jpg`** / **`poster_message.jpg`** — two stills from the film

**What it is:** "Pale Blue Dot" — a continuous 10-second zoom-out. We begin close on a living Earth — rotating, with drifting clouds, latitude-colored continents, a soft day/night terminator and glittering city lights on the night side — and pull back until the whole planet shrinks to a single pale blue point of light breathing in the dark. Over it, five quiet lines:

> EVERYONE YOU LOVE, — EVERYONE YOU HAVE EVER KNOWN, — EVERY HUMAN WHO HAS EVER LIVED — LIVED HERE. — BE KIND. IT'S THE ONLY HOME WE'VE GOT.

A slow ambient drone (low A partials, synthesized in pure Python) with two soft bell notes arriving with the final line, then silence and fade-out.

**Why this animation, of all possible ones:** the "overview effect" is one of the most reliably documented shifts in human perspective — seeing Earth whole, from outside, reliably increases compassion, humility, and concern for the collective. This piece is designed to induce a miniature of that effect in anyone, in ten seconds, regardless of language, politics, or beliefs — and then leaves them with one actionable sentence.

**How it was made** (`src/render.py`, pure stdlib + ffmpeg, no packages): a hand-drawn 72×36 ASCII world map sampled onto an orthographic sphere with bilinear smoothing; value-noise cloud layers rotating slightly faster than the surface; Lambert shading with a soft terminator; 700 seeded city lights on the night side; a 5×7 bitmap font with a box-blur glow for the captions; 340 twinkling stars; exponential zoom-out easing into a gaussian "pale dot" halo. Frames stream as raw RGB into ffmpeg's libx264 (with fade in/out), audio synthesized to WAV and muxed as AAC.
